steps.text: Line two baking sheets with waxed paper.

In a large pot or Dutch oven, combine butter, water and sugar. Bring to a boil. Boil 4 minutes; remove from heat. Introduce popcorn and stir to coat evenly. Pour onto prepared baking sheets and let cool before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweetened Popcorn
raw_recipe.description: Butter-flavored popcorn is coated with a simple syrup for a sweet treat.

review.reviewBody: This was exactly what I was looking for: cheap, easy and simple. My kids thought it was very yummy. Like other readers I did 1/2 cup brown sugar and 1/2 cup white sugar. I also added a half teaspoon vanilla after the 4 minutes of cooking, and 1/4 teaspoon salt, (because I used plain popcorn. I will definitely make this recipe again.

I made 3 bags of microwave popcorn.

I put the following ingredients in a microwave safe bowl:
3 (1/4) cups of water, 4 tablespoons of butter, 1 1/2 cups of white sugar, 1 teaspoon of vanilla extract, 1/4 cup of white cornsyrup, and a handful of chopped walnuts.

Microwave for 3 minutes at a time, remove & stir. Do this till mixture boils. (About 3 times).

Put popcorn in very large bowl. Pour mixture over popcorn & mix well with a rubber spatula.

The recipe is a perfect guide! I did what others did 1/2 brown sugar 1/2 plain ol'white sugar and added 1/4 tsp of vanilla to kick it up a notch. For those of you using the microwave popcorn I'd use 2 bags so coverage is not too thick...this recipe is SWEET...but to each his own. Also, def bake for 10-15min at 300 degrees. Makes a huge difference in the "crunch" quality. Made it for my daughters party and it was a HIT!

I used a bag of extreme butter microwave popcorn, keeping the other ingredients the same. I used raw sugar & love the flavor it added. After I coated the popcorn I layed it out on a baking sheet sprayed w/ Pam & baked it @ 300 for 5 minutes, stirred & baked for another 5 minutes to crisp it up some. My hubby ate every last kernel!.

I followed the recipe mostly. I did follow the suggestion of others to add a lil vanilla. Also I popped a 1/4 cup of kernels. The kernels weren't coated enough to my liking, so I did a second batch of the topping. And poured OVER the popcorn. Much better... Delish!

My 3-yr-old twins loved this! I did 1/2 brown/white sugar; a splash of vanilla, and next time will add some food coloring. I spread plain air-popped popcorn on 2 silpats & just poured the sauce over the popcorn & mixed up on the mats. I didn't have a big enough bowl and it seemed to cover it pretty well. This one's a keeper!
way too much water, it made it gross. I found another recipe that works better using 2 tbsp butter, 2 tbsp brown sugar, and 2 tbsp corn syrup, heated until sugar dissolves then poured over bowl.

This was fantastic and quick! I did add about 1/2 tsp vanilla to the sugar sauce. I also popped regular popcorn and then buttered & salted it to try to approximate buttered microwave popcorn. I then removed as many of the "old maids" I could find so we didn't go crunching down on them. I found that by putting the popcorn in a LARGE bowl the sauce seemed pretty evenly distributed.

Ahhhh! What can I say! I Loved it,I have been looking for a recipe and the only time I get this is once a year at the fair.I am glad I found it. I just popped my corn in butter and some salt,decreased sugar to 3/4 cup, added a tsp vanilla,and added food coloring also. just like the fairs,Yummy! Thanks for the recipe.
It was meh… glad I tried it but will never make this again. If you are going to make it, do not over cook the sugar mixture, also add a teaspoon of vanilla extract.

My popcorn looked really pretty and this was really cheap to make..... thats the only positive things I can say about this recipe. I made this as written but added a teaspoon of vanilla extract. This way too sweet.... it was like eating nothing but sugar. I am going to try to make this one more time as its a cheap cute treat for my daughter's classmates. I am going to try to make this again today but I am going to use brown sugar and drizzle the syrup on the popcorn. I will post a follow up.
This was so delicious. The next time I make this, I think I will only add half of the popcorn to the sugar. And then mix all the popcorn together after the sugar cools down
Followed the recipe exactly and it was WAY TOO SWEET.
It was really good, but I feel like it would have been a lot better if the sugar hadn't crystallized in the pan.
It's granular, for some reason. Not sure why. I did half and half of white and brown sugar. But it tastes good and was easy. Will try again.
This was so good. Turned out well and was easy to make. I will be making this for the next girls movie night!
My sister loves this!!!
we doubled the amount of popcorn but left everything else in the recipe the same and it was a lot less sugary than with just the six cups of popcorn but still tasted good
I really liked this recipe and adding in the food coloring made it a really fun treat for the kids. Personally it was way to sweet for me but what kid doesn't love super sweet wacky colored popcorn!
Super Easy and the my little ones loved it. Add the food coloring while it is boiling. It cools super fast on just wax paper on the counter for munching. Great for Christmas.
